title: "A Healthy Zebra Not a Sick Horse": A Cultural Case Study of an Autistic Individual in the USA.
abstract: Social communication is a key domain at the intersection of culture, medicine, and psychiatry, particularly when communication is medicalized in diagnoses like "autism spectrum disorder" (ASD). Clinicians and scholars debate dominant medical model discourses of autism as well as grassroots neurodiversity perspectives. Increasing influence of neurodiversity perspectives has yielded increasing clinical and communication science studies considering diversity (not deficit) in communication. This cultural case study considers how one autistic young man in the USA orchestrates twenty-first-century discourses about autism, reflecting on his experiences with communication, social disconnect, and sensory sensitivities. His case illustrates how autistic-led concepts such as the "double-empathy problem," increased attention to sensory-social components of autism, and the changing role of the Internet have substantially reconfigured the voices that autistic adults orchestrate compared with those explicated by previous scholars. These reconfigurations align with changes in medical models of autism that blur and blend with neurodiversity models. His efforts to build supportive, autistic-led spaces provide models for authentic interaction and reveal new tools for forming biosocial autistic community. This cultural case study therefore reinforces the need to avoid one-size-fits-all approaches, and the importance of a person-centered approach to meet the needs of everyone within the community.

title: Unravelling the phylogenetic systematics of the horse-hoof limpets (Mollusca: Gastropoda: Hipponicidae).
abstract: Hipponicidae are a family of sedentary marine caenogastropod snails commonly known as "hoof limpets". They are characterized by cap-shaped shells, and most genera develop, in adulthood, a highly specialized foot along with a distinctive horseshoe-shaped internal muscle attachment, allowing them to attach permanently to hard substrates. Here we present the first comprehensive, molecular-based revision of Hipponicidae using both a Sanger (426 specimens, 4 loci) and a phylogenomic exon-capture based NGS approach (18 specimens, 528-864 loci), integrating results with morphological and ecological data. This is the first step in a substantial phylogenetic revision of hipponicid classification that has long been problematic due to extensive shell plasticity and morphological convergence with other limpet-like caenogastropods. We identified 61 putative species, approximately two thirds of which are new to science, including several complexes of cryptic species that in some cases involve type species of their respective genera. Molecular evidence supports a redefinition of at least half of the genera currently accepted. Hipponicids emerge as a lineage with extreme adaptations to a quasi-sessile adult lifestyle, with the bulk of species having a horseshoe-shaped foot muscle that has almost completely lost its locomotory function, and produced a calcareous plate cemented to the substrate. This family also spans a wide bathymetric range, yet with most lineages restricted to either shallow or deep waters. Ecological data further indicate there is variation among hipponicid genera, differing in the degree of flexibility in substrate- and host-selection, ranging from specialized to capable of colonising the surface of a wide range of living and non-living substrates, but in general having pronounced shell plasticity in response to attachment conditions.

title: Effect of pentoxifylline and of penicillamine, hypotaurine and epinephrine on motility of poor-motility frozen-thawed semen in stallions.
abstract: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) allows equine embryo production from low-quality semen. However, some frozen-thawed semen has such low motility that selection of motile sperm for injection is challenging. To explore methods to increase sperm motility to facilitate selection during ICSI, we evaluated the effects of pentoxifylline and of penicillamine, hypotaurine and epinephrine (PHE) on both standard frozen-thawed (1x) semen and a model of poor-motility semen (4x, frozen and thawed four times). In Exp. 1, 1x and 4x semen was treated with 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 mg/mL pentoxifylline; in Exp. 2, 1x and 4x semen was treated with 2 or 4 mg/mL pentoxifylline, or with low or high concentrations of PHE (18 µM penicillamine, 9 µM hypotaurine and 1.8 µM epinephrine, or twice this concentration). Semen from three stallions was used for each experiment. Total (TMOT) and progressive (PMOT) motility were assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis, and data analyzed using the Friedman test with pairwise Wilcoxon tests. In Exp. 1, pentoxifylline had no significant effect on motility of 1x semen, but increased TMOT and PMOT of 4x semen in a dose-dependent manner (P < 0.05). In Exp. 2, pentoxifylline significantly increased PMOT at 0 and 30 min for 1x semen, and TMOT and PMOT up to two hours in 4x semen. In an exploratory trial, ICSI with pentoxifylline-treated sperm yielded a 37% blastocyst rate (4/11), vs. 30% (3/10) for control sperm. We conclude that PTX, but not PHE, may have application to increase motility during selection of sperm for ICSI.

title: Physiological and fertility responses to alternative puberty induction strategies and fixed-time artificial insemination protocols in Bos indicus replacement heifers.
abstract: Three experiments were conducted to characterize the endocrine and ovarian responses associated with alternative puberty induction strategies and determine their impact on fertility of Bos indicus replacement heifers. In experiment (Exp.) 1, prepubertal heifers (n = 32) were assigned to either no treatment (CTRL), an intravaginal progesterone (P4) device (IVD) for 11 d, or a 150-mg long-acting P4 injection (iP4). Blood samples were collected daily from Days 0 to 12 to determine circulating P4 concentrations. In Exp. 2, heifers without a corpus luteum (CL; n = 629) were assigned to CTRL, 12 days of IVD with estradiol cypionate (ECP) at IVD removal (IVD + ECP), or iP4 followed by ECP 12 days later (iP4+ECP). All heifers were exposed to the same fixed-time artificial insemination (FTAI) protocol. In Exp. 3, all heifers (n = 2136) received the same IVD + ECP puberty induction protocol described in Exp. 2, followed by a 9-day P4-based FTAI protocol consisting of estradiol benzoate on Day 0, ECP and equine chorionic gonadotropin at IVD removal on Day 9, and FTAI on Day 11. Heifers were randomly assigned to receive prostaglandin F2α either on Day 9 (CTRL) or on Days -12 and 7 (PG). In Exp. 1, IVD generated greater and more stable circulating P4 concentrations than iP4 throughout treatment (P < 0.01). In Exp. 2, IVD + ECP and iP4+ECP similarly increased the percentage of heifers with a CL at initiation of the FTAI protocol compared with CTRL (P < 0.01). However, pregnancy rates to FTAI were greater in IVD + ECP compared with both CTRL and iP4+ECP heifers (P ≤ 0.05). In Exp. 3, PG decreased the proportion of heifers with a CL on Day 9 and increased follicle diameter, estrus expression, and pregnancy rates compared with CTRL (P < 0.01). Improvements in estrus expression and pregnancy rates were greater in heifers with a CL present at completion of the puberty induction protocol. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that use of an IVD for puberty induction and strategic administration of PG improved the fertility of Bos indicus replacement heifers subjected to FTAI.

title: Treatment of Relapsed/Refractory Aplastic Anemia.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Relapsed or refractory aplastic anemia (AA) remains a challenging clinical scenario despite significant advances in first-line therapy. AA is an immune-mediated bone marrow failure characterized by pancytopenia and hypocellular marrow. In adult patients, first-line immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with horse antithymocyte globulin (ATG) plus cyclosporine A (CsA) achieves hematologic response rates of 60-80%, but 10-30% of severe AA cases will relapse after initial improvement, and a similar fraction may be refractory to initial therapy. Management of relapsed/refractory AA (R/R AA) requires a comprehensive, patient-tailored approach incorporating both pharmacologic therapies and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Advances in the past decade have expanded treatment options. Second-line IST (e.g. repeat ATG or alemtuzumab) can rescue ~ 30-60% of patients, while the thrombopoietin receptor agonist eltrombopag has shown response rates around 40-60% in refractory AA. Newer TPO-agonists such as avatrombopag and romiplostim have demonstrated similar efficacy with favorable safety. Allogeneic HSCT remains the only curative therapy, and outcomes have improved markedly even for older patients and alternative donors. Salvage HSCT yields long-term failure-free survival superior to medical therapy in appropriate candidates, with 4-year overall survival ~ 80% in recent series. Notably, haploidentical donor HSCT with post-transplant cyclophosphamide has emerged as a viable option for patients lacking matched donors, achieving 1-year survival ~ 81% with minimal graft-vs-host disease (GVHD). Pediatric considerations include a lower threshold for upfront transplantation and unique supportive care needs. This review examines the current evidence (2017-2025) for treating R/R AA, including mechanisms of action of therapies, patient selection, outcomes, and adverse effects. We highlight real-world data, clinical trial results, and global perspectives (with a focus on resource-limited settings like India) to guide optimal management of relapsed or refractory AA in both adults and children.

title: Anti Thymocyte Globulin- Development.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Anti thymocyte globulin (ATG) is a polyclonal antibody primarily derived from rabbit, horse, or porcine sources, used to prevent or treat T-cell-mediated rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), and aplastic anaemia (AA). It has demonstrated efficacy in reducing both acute and chronic GVHD and improving graft survival in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and solid organ transplant settings without affecting overall survival. Mechanistically, ATG depletes T-cells, modulates myeloid cells via PDL1 induction, and induces immune regulation. Rabbit ATG (rATG) is commonly used in organ transplants and HSCT. Horse or equine ATG (eATG) has proven efficacy in haematological disorders, particularly AA. Indigenous eATG (Thymogam) is widely used as part of immunosuppressive therapy (IST) in AA. Porcine ATG (pATG) is emerging as a therapeutic alternative in AA. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) has potential to improve dosing precision and immune reconstitution. Future directions focus on optimizing dosing, personalization and expanding indications. Manufacturing of ATG is complex process and requires multilevel monitoring and quality control to ensure efficacy and safety of the products for human use. This article aims to summarise the developmental evolution, composition, mechanism of action, overview of clinical uses of ATG, dosing, administration, and monitoring strategies, including the role of TDM and a brief description of the manufacturing process and various quality aspects of ATGs for clinical use.

title: Thrombopoietin Receptor Agonists Therapy in Aplastic Anaemia.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Immune-mediated aplastic anaemia (IAA) remains a life-threatening disorder characterized by immune-driven bone marrow failure and consequent cytopenias. Frontline therapy includes immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with horse antithymocyte globulin (h-ATG) or rabbit ATG (r-ATG) in combination with cyclosporine, or allogeneic stem cell transplantation in eligible patients. Despite these approaches, overall response rates (ORR) to IST remain at approximately 60-70%,(Complete Responses ~20-30%, Partial Responses~30-40%) with relapse and refractoriness posing major clinical challenges. Attempts to intensify IST using agents such as cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, sirolimus, alemtuzumab, or prolonged cyclosporine(CSA) have shown limited additional benefit, suggesting that inadequate marrow reserve rather than persistent autoreactivity may underlie refractoriness. Over the past decade, thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) have emerged as important therapeutic options for IAA, demonstrating single-agent activity as well as synergistic efficacy when combined with ATG and cyclosporine. Their mechanistic rationale extends beyond megakaryopoiesis. TPO receptors are expressed on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and TPO-RAs may enhance stem-cell viability, promote multilineage hematologic recovery, and increase marrow cellularity. Additionally, TPO-RAs may modulate immune tolerance by expanding regulatory B and T cells, attenuating macrophage activity, and impairing dendritic-cell maturation, thereby helping to rebalance immune dysregulation. Eltrombopag(EPAG) and romiplostim are the most extensively studied TPO-RAs in IAA. Eltrombopag, an oral small-molecule TPO-RA, has demonstrated efficacy in both frontline and refractory IAA, with good hematologic recovery and potential iron-chelating effects. Romiplostim, a peptibody, has been primarily used in patients with refractory disease. Their distinct pharmacokinetic and safety profiles, including concerns about hepatotoxicity with eltrombopag and potential risks of clonal evolution with long-term TPO-RA exposure, require careful clinical consideration. Prospective studies, including the NIH cohort and the RACE trial, have provided pivotal evidence that adding a TPO-RA to standard IST improves hematologic responses and supports enhanced multilineage recovery with acceptable safety. However, rates of relapse and clonal evolution remain comparable to historical cohorts. Ongoing studies aim to refine optimal sequencing, dosing strategies, and combination regimens. The evolving evidence supports the integration of TPO-RAs into IAA management to augment marrow recovery and achieve more durable correction of cytopenias.

title: Nociceptive thresholds and beta-endorphin concentrations in horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction: a cross-sectional comparative study.
abstract: Increased beta-endorphin (β-END) concentrations in horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID) are hypothesized to lead to increased pain tolerance of affected horses, however, alteration of nociceptive thresholds (NTs) in PPID horses has not been investigated previously. Evaluate whether NTs differ between horses with PPID and controls and whether β-END concentrations correlate with NTs. Fifty equids aged 19-32 years. Cross-sectional comparative study conducted in February 2025. The study included a PPID group (n = 24 horses) and a control group (n = 26 horses). Both groups were subjected to mechanical and thermal stimulation, and NTs were recorded. Plasma adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and β-END concentrations were quantified, and the association between β-END concentrations and NTs was analyzed. Although β-END concentrations were higher in the PPID group (482 [316-735] pg/mL [geometric mean (95% confidence interval [CI])]) compared with controls (47.8 [23.0-53.4] pg/mL [geometric mean (95% CI)]; P < .001), no correlation between β-END concentrations and NTs was found. Furthermore, no significant group differences and correlations were found for mechanical (MNTs) and thermal nociceptive thresholds (TNTs). In this selected cohort of older horses without clinically relevant pain, horses with PPID did not exhibit increased NTs compared to controls. Although β-END concentrations were higher in horses with PPID, no association between β-END concentrations and NTs was identified. These findings do not support a measurable effect of increased circulating β-END concentrations on NTs in the study cohort.

title: The quality of the horse-rider relationship and mental well-being in female equestrian riders: a cross-sectional validation study in Hungary.
journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
abstract: The horse-rider relationship is increasingly recognized as a determinant of psychological well-being in equestrian riders, yet validated instruments remain scarce outside English-speaking contexts. This study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Horse-Rider Relationship Scale (HRRS) and its associations with mental well-being in Hungarian female equestrian riders. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 160 female equestrian riders in Hungary. Participants completed the HRRS-measuring compatibility, communication, respect, trust, and self-confidence-and the Sport Mental Health Continuum Short Form. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and Pearson correlations were conducted; group differences by horse ownership were also examined. The CFA confirmed the five-factor structure with acceptable fit (CFI = .974, TLI = .962, RMSEA = .059, SRMR = .037). Horse ownership was not associated with any HRRS dimension. All five relationship dimensions yielded significant positive correlations with emotional, psychological, and social well-being, with the strongest associations found for self-confidence (r = 0.495) and communication (r = 0.485) with psychological well-being. The HRRS demonstrates sound psychometric properties in a Hungarian female equestrian sample. Relationship quality-rather than horse ownership-is associated with greater mental well-being, underscoring the importance of fostering the horse-rider bond in both sport and therapeutic equestrian contexts.

title: Guttural Pouch Endoscopy Outperforms Radiography for Detection of Advanced Temporohyoid Osteoarthropathy Using Computed Tomography as the Reference Standard in 382 Horses.
journal: Veterinary radiology & ultrasound : the official journal of the American College of Veterinary Radiology and the International Veterinary Radiology Association
abstract: Temporohyoid osteoarthropathy (THO) is a chronic, non-septic disorder of the equine temporohyoid joint (THJ) that may lead to neurological dysfunction. Computed tomography (CT) has become the gold standard in the assessment of THO. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of guttural pouch endoscopy and radiography with CT as the reference standard in horses with THO. Medical records and imaging data from 382 horses (764 THJ) were reviewed. All 382 horses underwent CT examination, with endoscopic examinations available either uni- or bilaterally, and radiographs performed in 107 of the 382 horses (28.0%). CT studies, radiographs, and endoscopic videos were blinded, reviewed, and graded by two observers. THO (CT grade ≥ 1) was identified in 147 horses (38.5%). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for CT (prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa [PABAK] = 0.89-0.93), moderate for endoscopic scoring (PABAK = 0.46-0.51), and almost perfect for radiographic evaluation (PABAK = 0.81-0.90). Sensitivity and specificity of guttural pouch endoscopy for the diagnosis of THO (CT Grade 3-5) were 81.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 67.7%-94.8%) to 84.9% (95% CI: 72.6%-97.1%), and 87.6% (95% CI: 83.8%-91.4%) to 90.7% (95% CI: 87.4%-94.0%), respectively. An endoscopic score ≥2 significantly correlated with CT-confirmed cases of moderate-to-severe THO. Radiography showed the lowest diagnostic accuracy and was limited to severe cases of THO. In conclusion, guttural pouch endoscopy is a valuable first-line examination for identifying advanced (CT Grade 3-5) THO. Radiography has limited diagnostic utility, and CT showed a high interobserver agreement.

title: Crystal Structure of Equine Coronavirus Main Protease in Complex with the inhibitor GC376-Considerations for Pan-Coronaviral Inhibitor Design.
abstract: Coronaviruses are highly transmissible pathogens that infect a broad range of hosts, with some causing severe illness in both humans and animals. Considerable research effort for the treatment of acute infection has been directed towards human coronaviral targets, including SARS-CoV-1/-2, MERS-CoV and other human coronaviruses. However, comparable study of related animal coronaviruses that may cross-over to humans is less prominent. Here we describe the cloning, isolation and purification of the genomically proposed equine coronavirus main protease (EqCoV-Mpro) and its C59S and C225S mutants to facilitate drug development. FDA-approved and investigational SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors, including GC376, inhibit EqCoV-Mpro with nanomolar potency. A surface-cysteine C59S mutation enabled the first X-ray co-crystal structure of EqCoV Mpro with GC376 at 2.0 Å. It reveals a deeper, more hydrophobic active site than related human and animal CoV Mpros, favoring compact inhibitors and informing future pan-coronaviral inhibitor design.

title: Behavioural sleep quality and quantity and their associations with age, salivary cortisol and abnormal behaviours: A preliminary field study in racing thoroughbreds.
abstract: Sleep plays a key role in both physical recovery and welfare. However, sleep patterns remain poorly documented in animals, particularly in athletic horses. This study aimed to provide a detailed description of sleep quantity and quality in training Thoroughbred racehorses and to investigate their relationships with age, abnormal behaviours, and cortisol. Thirteen Thoroughbreds (2-7 years old) were continuously monitored in their home environment for 48 hours. An ethogram was used to quantify sleep-related behaviours associated with the two main behavioural sleep states: non-rapid eye movement (NREM-like) and rapid eye movement (REM-like), as well as sleep interruptions (from day 1 at 12:00 to day 3 at 12:00). Sleep Quality Indices (SQIs), reflecting the relationship between sleep duration and sleep interruptions (SIs), were then calculated. Behavioural observations of four indicators of poor welfare (alertness, stereotypies, inactivity, aggressiveness towards humans) were performed using scan sampling, and salivary cortisol was measured each morning. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess the links between sleep quantity and quality, age, mean cortisol, and abnormal behaviours. Age was significantly associated with behavioural sleep quantity, being positively associated with total behavioural NREM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 5.40, p = 0.02), and negatively associated with total behavioural REM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 4.36, p = 0.04) and total recumbency duration (Wald test: χ2 = 5.68, p = 0.02). Morning cortisol concentrations were negatively associated with Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.26, p = 0.02) and Combined SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.60, p = 0.02). Likewise, horses displaying abnormal behaviours more frequently had lower Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 4.07, p = 0.04), pointing to a potential link between stress or altered welfare and poorer sleep quality. These findings suggest that, whilst the type and duration of equine behavioural-related sleep may be mainly affected by age, sleep quality is associated with both cortisol levels and the expression of abnormal behaviours, indicating that poor sleep quality may be linked to poor welfare in this population of horses. Overall, these findings highlight behavioural sleep quality as a potential component of racehorse welfare assessment and warrant further investigation into the factors influencing sleep in athletic horses.

title: Forb Communities and Plant Functional Traits Differ Between Horse Grazed Pastures and Abandoned Fields in Northern Sweden.
abstract: Seminatural grasslands, created by traditional land use systems such as low-intensity cattle grazing, have high ecological value due to the occurrence of numerous plant species and their associated faunal communities. In Sweden, this habitat is threatened by both land abandonment and agricultural intensification. Low-intensity grazing by large herbivores could potentially benefit grassland-associated forb communities. The aim of this study was to compare the forb communities between horse-grazed pastures and abandoned fields in the boreal region of Northern Sweden. We surveyed forbs within 20 horse-grazed pastures and 20 abandoned fields, and compared community composition, diversity, and trait composition. Within the horse-grazed pastures, we analyzed the effect of grazing intensity, mowing frequency, and number of years grazed. The composition of the forb community differed between horse pastures and abandoned fields. Forb species richness tended to be higher in horse-grazed pastures, which were dominated by ruderal species associated with grazing, while forb communities in abandoned fields consisted mainly of competitive species. Eight species associated with semi-natural pastures were found, primarily within horse pastures. Forb species in horse pastures had a lower canopy height and seed mass, which are two known traits associated with grazing. On the contrary, the specific leaf area (SLA), a trait associated with tolerance to grazing, tended to be higher among the forbs of abandoned fields. The number of wind-pollinated species was lower in fields that were grazed for a longer time and a positive trend was shown for total forb species richness. Pastures with higher grazing intensity had lower seed mass. Synthesis: Horse-grazed pastures hosted ruderal, grazing-associated plant communities compared to abandoned sites which were dominated by strong competitors. Our results show that horse-grazed pastures host a plant community with short, small-seeded plants. The differences between field types indicate that horse grazing might be a potential restoration method to provide habitat for grazing-associated forbs which are disfavoured by land abandonment.

title: Can a 3D Printed Chondrograft Implant Offer a Solution for Full Thickness Cartilage Lesions in an Equine Preclinical Model?
journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society
abstract: Articular cartilage defects have limited ability to heal resulting in fibrocartilage that is functionally and structurally inferior to hyaline cartilage. The aim of this study was to validate the Chondrograft Implant for full thickness cartilage lesion treatment, assessing its ability to fill the defect and support repair tissue engraftment. Bilateral 15 mm diameter cartilage defects were created on the lateral trochlear ridge of the femur in 12 skeletally mature horses. One defect was treated with the implant while the contralateral limb was an empty control defect. Horses were exercised starting at week 4 and study end points were at 36-weeks for 4 horses and 52-weeks for 8 horses. Lameness examinations were performed every 4 weeks and arthroscopic recheck surgeries were performed at 12-weeks. Post-mortem evaluation included macroscopic appearance, MRI, histology and biomechanical testing. Clinical, ICRS, MRI and gross morphology outcomes were compared between groups using parametric or non-parametric tests as appropriate. Mechanical stiffness was compared between groups using two-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc. There was no difference in lameness between control or treated limbs (p > 0.5). The 12-week arthroscopy showed treated defects had significantly improved fill (99% vs 42%, p < 0.0001) and ICRS scores (11.3 ± 1.1 vs 4.1 ± 3.1, p < 0.0001). Endpoint ICRS grade at 52- weeks was significantly better in the treated defect compared to the control defect scoring (3.75 ± 2.25 vs 9.125 ± 2.25, p = 0.0005). Biomechanical testing revealed significantly improved repair tissue stiffness in treated defects compared to controls (p < 0.0001). Chondrograft implants resulted in excellent defect filling with biomechanical function similar to normal healthy articular cartilage.

title: Surveillance of Culicoides (Diptera: Ceratopogonidae) during the 2020 African horse sickness outbreak in Thailand: Species identification and African horse sickness virus detection.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
abstract: During African horse sickness (AHS) outbreak in Thailand in 2020, Culicoides vector surveillance was conducted to determine Culicoides species associated with the disease transmission. Ultraviolet light traps were set up to collect Culicoides midges at 17 affected and 2 vaccinated sites. A total of 28,226 Culicoides were collected and morphologically identified into 15 species from 6 subgenera and 1 species group. The most abundance species was C. oxystoma (37.37%), followed by C. imicola (24.09%), the main vector of AHS, and C. innoxius (15%). Molecular identification by DNA barcoding of mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunit I gene (COI) confirmed 11 species, including an additional species, C. similis. AHS virus RNA was detected by real-time RT-PCR in 8 of 280 pools tested (6 pools of C. oxystoma and 2 pools of C. imicola collected from zebra farms). This study provides a comprehensive, multi-site characterization of Culicoides species composition and abundance during the 2020 African horse sickness outbreak in Thailand, combining morphological and molecular (COI) identification. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first entomological survey of Culicoides species associated with zebra in Thailand, and additionally reports the first COI reference sequence for C. similis collected from horse farms in this country.

title: First case report of lameness due to Halicephalobus gingivalis in the cannon bone of a horse in France.
journal: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
abstract: Halicephalobus gingivalis is a free-living nematode that sporadically infects the central nervous system of equids. Cases of H. gingivalis in France are scarce and mostly associated with neurological signs. This paper documents a first case of lameness due to H. gingivalis in the cannon bone of a horse. Acute onset of lameness of the right leg associated with a painful swelling did not improve under nonsteroid anti-inflammatory treatment. X-rays revealed proliferative and osteolytic lesions. Post-mortem histology revealed the presence of H. gingivalis in the cannon bone. The case confirms the great variety of the clinical signs associated with H. gingivalis infection which should be included in the differential of acute foreleg lameness in horses.

title: Preliminary evaluation of heart rates and body measurements of UK heavy draft breeds, using a novel visual body condition score.
abstract: Most UK heavy draft breeds are registered as 'At Risk' or higher by the Rare Breed Survival Trust. Although mainly used for showing competitions, their size predisposes them to musculoskeletal and cardiac issues, yet there is very little data published on the physiological demands and body morphology in these breeds. The aim of this study was to assess differences in visual body condition, body morphometry and heart rates between different UK draft-breed horses when exercised at home and at shows METHODS: A longitudinal study design collected data on adult UK draft horses (Shire n=92; Clydesdale n=38; Percheron n=34; Suffolk-Punch n=49; males n=114; females n=99; mean age 7.32±3.95s.d.), at home (n=213) and a proportion of those (n=167) at shows (2021-2022). Body morphometrics, visual Body Condition Score (vBCS: scale 1-6 adapted for draft horses), heart rates (HR, rest and post exercise) were measured, and competition placings recorded, once for each horse. More Suffolk-Punch and Shire horses scored as overweight (43% and 31% respectively) or obese (30% and 13%) compared to the other breeds. Suffolk-Punch were less high (1.74m ±5.4 s.d.) versus all others (mean 182±6 s.d.) with a greater neck circumference than other breeds (P<0.01, Anova, Bonferroni). When at home, resting HRs (bpm) ranged from 40-42 (±2.9s.d), HRs post a set exercise test ranged from 103 to 111 (±8s.d.), and at shows post show ring from 105-112 (±8.7s.d.), indicating very low workloads. In-hand horses had significantly higher HRs and higher vBCS in comparison to ridden horses. At shows, higher vBCS presented higher likelihood of 1st-placings (P<0.01, rho=0.65) with 94% of 1st-placed horses overweight (37%) or obese (60%). This study provides a vital preliminary insight into the health and work status of UK draft breed horses. These horses had low fitness requirements and a large proportion was above the ideal body condition score, which was favoured by judges. The vBCS has potential to be used by show judges in the future.

title: Corrigendum to Evaluation of a canine Coll2-1 ELISA kit for use in equine serum and its correlation with radiographic joint disease, Journal of Equine Veterinary Science 166 (2026) 106063.
Cavitation-governed antimicrobial synergy of ultrasound and essential oil nanoemulsions: A mechanistic review.
abstract: Ultrasound-assisted essential-oil nanoemulsions are a promising green strategy for food preservation, yet a unified framework linking cavitation physics, antimicrobial action, and food-matrix effects is still lacking. This review integrates advances from 2020 to 2025 to propose a cavitation-driven "Sword and Trojan Horse" model in which acoustic energy is converted into coupled mechanical and chemical functionalities. Inertial cavitation ("Sword") generates microjets, shock waves, and radicals that transiently permeabilize microbial membranes, while nanoemulsions ("Trojan Horse") deliver essential-oil bioactives intracellularly. Viscosity, interfacial heterogeneity, and endogenous antioxidants modulate cavitation intensity, radical lifetime, and droplet-cell interactions, dictating efficacy. Beyond antimicrobial action, cavitation orchestrates the structuring of biopolymer active-packaging films by controlling droplet organization, interfacial stability, and release kinetics. Emerging evidence extends the framework to include ferroptosis-like lipid peroxidation pathways via ultrasound-enhanced Fenton chemistry. Persistent limitations include the predominance of low-frequency (≈20 kHz) systems, limited cavitation mapping in real food matrices, a lack of standardized sonochemical dosimetry, and scarce pilot-scale validation. Addressing these gaps is crucial for predictive, scalable process design. Collectively, ultrasound-nanoemulsion systems are positioned as cavitation-engineered platforms for antimicrobial control, food structuring, and next-generation sustainable preservation.

title: Neuropathology of early-onset equine neuroaxonal dystrophy and concurrent infectious disease in two related Andalusian colts.
abstract: Equine neuroaxonal dystrophy (eNAD) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to a genetic predisposition and vitamin E deficiency, typically appearing in the first year of life. We document the clinical and pathological characteristics of early-onset eNAD in two related Andalusian colts with atypical severe neurological presentations. Following a normal birth, the colts intermittently displayed abnormal postures; either head between the forelimbs or hindlimbs extended caudally, abnormal ambulation or loss of balance and recumbency. At necropsy, colt 1 had omphaloarteritis, urachal cystitis, pulmonary oedema, hydropericardium, peritoneal effusion, enterocolitis and oesophagitis. Colt 2 had purulent bronchopneumonia affecting the caudomedial-ventral left lung. Bacterial cultures isolated Arthrobacter sp, Pseudomonas sp and Enterococcus mundtii from peritoneal effusion (colt 1), and Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus, Streptococcus gallolyticus and Enterococcus gallinarum from purulent lung exudate (colt 2). In both colts, there were acute neurodegenerative changes in the brain and spinal cord characterized by bilateral symmetrical neuroaxonal degeneration, chromatolysis and loss of neurones. These were most severe at the cuneate and gracilis nuclei, and the dorsal corticospinal nuclei at T9. Both colts were vitamin E deficient. A diagnosis of septicaemia from ascending umbilical infection and early-onset eNAD and concurrent pulmonary streptococcosis and eNAD were made in colts 1 and 2, respectively. Similar clinical history in the colts' full sibling from 2024 supports an underlying genetic aetiology for eNAD. This severe neurological presentation is atypical for classical eNAD in related foals, is unlikely attributed to septicaemia or pulmonary streptococcosis and therefore warrants further investigation in the Andalusian breed.

title: The Evolution of Total Ankle Replacement Design: Are We Putting the Cart Before the Horse?: Commentary on an article by Jensen K. Henry, MD, et al.: "Implant Choice Impacts Initial Tibial Component Micromotion in Total Ankle Replacement. A Biomechanical Analysis".
journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume

title: A Trojan Horse Nanotrap with a GSH-Responsive Molecular Gate Orchestrates Ferroptosis via Coupled Iron Release and Spatial GPX4 Inhibition.
abstract: Disruption of the dynamic equilibrium between ferroptotic execution pathways and cellular defense mechanisms can trigger ferroptosis, providing a compelling strategy for tumor suppression and the circumvention of drug resistance. Here, we engineered a Trojan Horse-inspired nanotrap, MIPGPX4@aMOF@CM, that integrates biomimetic recognition, redox-responsive amorphous MOF (aMOF) chemistry, and molecular imprinting to disrupt metal homeostasis and disable key protective pathways, thereby triggering cascade-amplified ferroptosis. The inner core is a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) that selectively recognizes GPX4, while the outer shell consists of a novel iron-based aMOF acting as a redox-activated molecular gate and is further cloaked with a cancer cell membrane. This multifunctional nanoplatform enables tumor-specific iron delivery and spatially controlled GPX4 inhibition. Upon homotypic membrane-mediated tumor targeting and cellular internalization, elevated intracellular glutathione (GSH) triggers aMOF degradation, leading to GSH depletion, iron release, and on-demand exposure of the imprinted GPX4 binding sites. This gate-controlled cascade synergistically promotes Fenton chemistry and GPX4 inactivation, substantially disrupting the balance between ferroptotic execution and antioxidant defenses and enhancing tumor-selective ferroptotic responses. Collectively, this work highlights that precisely orchestrating metal homeostasis, redox regulation, and GPX4 inhibition represents a promising strategy for precision ferroptosis-based cancer therapy.

title: Draft genome sequence of an equine-associated Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium strain YAH-H10 harboring an IncHI2A plasmid carrying mcr-9.1 and blaSHV-12.
abstract: Horses are recognized as important reservoirs of Salmonella. Here, we report the draft genome sequences of Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium isolates recovered from a hospitalized horse in Kentucky, USA, carrying the plasmid-mediated colistin resistance gene mcr-9.1 together with extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) genes, including blaSHV-12.

title: Equine herpesvirus-1 molecular prevalence and serological status of healthy broodmares in southern ontario.
abstract: Equine herpesvirus-1 is associated with abortion as well as respiratory disease and myeloencephalopathy. Vaccination is frequently used to mitigate the associated diseases and limit virus spread, but no studies have reported on the serological status of Ontario's broodmare population or the response to vaccination. We hypothesize that Ontario broodmares have a high anti-EHV-1 titer due to vaccination and exposure, but that these titres are not affected by pregnancy status. Further, we suspect that even though two vaccines are labeled as aids in the protection against EHV-1-associated abortion, they produce similar immune responses and affect viral shedding as other EHV-1 vaccines used in a natural population. Sera were collected from 381 healthy broodmares from 42 Ontario farms bi-monthly from December 2016 through October 2017. Blood, nasal, and vaginal swab samples for EHV-1 droplet digital PCR analysis were also collected every two months, as well as demographic surveys and vaccination information. Serology was assessed using virus neutralization and ELISA for IgGa (IgG1), IgGb (IgG4/7), and IgG(T) (IgG3/5). Titers significantly varied by breed/breed group, but differences varied by serological measure. Titers increased with age but were not affected by pregnancy status. Most mares had EHV-1 specific IgG and virus neutralizing (VN) titers but 32.3 % did have neutralizing titers < 1:512, and 42.1 % of vaccinated mares had no biologically significant changes in their neutralizing titers during the study period. IgG subisotype levels varied with the vaccine product, but not in a consistent pattern across subisotypes. No IgG subisotype was significantly associated with EHV-1 detection. In summary, vaccination was associated with increased titers regardless of type of vaccine used, no vaccine product produced a consistent immune response, and a fraction of mares did not respond to commercial vaccines despite regular vaccination, and titer levels were not predictive of EHV-1 detection.

title: Clinical characterization of extrapyramidal reactions to metoclopramide and bromopride in healthy horses: a pilot safety-based study.
abstract: Benzamide prokinetics are widely used in horses, but extrapyramidal adverse reactions are reported, with limited information regarding their early clinical presentation and temporal evolution. Bromopride is used empirically, but equine neurological safety data are lacking. To characterize the clinical and temporal evolution of extrapyramidal reactions following intramuscular administration of metoclopramide and bromopride in healthy horses. A prospective pilot safety-based dose de-escalation study followed by a randomized crossover phase was conducted in five healthy adult geldings. Horses received intramuscular metoclopramide (MET) or bromopride (BRO). Higher doses were progressively reduced according to observed clinical responses. At lowest doses, all horses received MET, BRO, and control in a randomized crossover design. Horses were monitored for neurological, behavioral, and autonomic signs for 24 h. Extrapyramidal reactions occurred in all horses receiving 0.3 mg/kg MET and BRO at 0.2, 0.1, and 0.05 mg/kg. At the lowest evaluated doses, reactions occurred in 1/5 horses after MET (0.125 mg/kg) and 0/5 after BRO (0.025 mg/kg). In horses in which reactions progressed, early manifestations, including restlessness, muscle tension, repetitive jaw movements, and autonomic activation, preceded more pronounced signs such as compulsive locomotor activity, dystonic postures, marked agitation, and attempts to climb or jump. Signs developed within approximately 10-60 min, lasted 30-60 min, and resolved spontaneously within 1-2 h. In healthy adult horses, intramuscular metoclopramide and bromopride produced extrapyramidal reactions at several evaluated doses. Progressive or severe manifestations followed early behavioral and motor abnormalities, although early manifestations did not invariably progress to more pronounced reactions.

title: Does Horse Castration Impact Osteoarticular Metabolism?
abstract: Castration is a common breeding practice in equines, primarily used to reduce the fiery and sometimes aggressive temperament of stallions by removing the primary source of sex steroid hormones, particularly testosterone. In several species, steroid hormones are known to play a key role in achieving peak bone mass during puberty and maintaining skeletal homeostasis in adulthood. Indeed, clinical studies in men with testicular failure have reported an increased risk of osteoporosis. To our knowledge, the relationship between testicular steroidogenesis and bone metabolism in adult horses remains poorly understood. There is no consensus among veterinarians and breeders regarding the optimal timing of castration, horses are castrated at various stages of life. This lack of knowledge led us to investigate the effect of castration performed either after puberty or during adulthood on equine osteoarticular metabolism. Circulating biomarkers of cartilage and bone metabolism (CTX-I, N-MID, CTX-II, CP-II, COMP, and HA), inflammatory markers (PGE2 and IL-6), and steroid hormones (testosterone and estradiol) were quantified in blood samples collected over a 9-month period following castration in horses castrated after period puberty or in adulthood. Castration, whether performed after puberty or in adulthood, resulted in drastic fall in testosterone and estradiol levels. However, this hormonal decline had no impact on osteoarticular metabolism or on inflammatory markers. Overall, our results demonstrate that bone and cartilage homeostasis in horses are maintained independently of gonadal steroids. Interestingly, circulating steroid levels remained detectable after castration suggesting the existence of extragonadal steroid sources in horses and warranting further investigation into their origin.

title: Letter to the editor: Comments on 'Multi-centre clinical audit of oxygen and inhalant anaesthetic usage in equine anaesthesia: The potential benefits of training and low-flow techniques'.
Identification of mineral microparticles accumulated in equine lung tissue: Is there a link between the environment and the development of interstitial lung disease? A case-control study.
abstract: Several non-infectious and infectious causes are linked to the development of equine fibrosing interstitial lung disease (EqF-ILD); although many cases remain idiopathic. It is not known whether inhaled mineral microparticles, as in humans, contribute to EqF-ILD. (1) To assess the presence, nature, and proportion of environmental mineral microparticles in lung tissue of equids with EqF-ILD compared with controls and (2) to identify environmental variables potentially associated with mineral microparticle accumulation. Prospective-retrospective case-control study. Paraffin-embedded lung tissue blocks from 21 equids previously diagnosed with EqF-ILD (EMPF/idiopathic) and lung samples prospectively collected from 10 healthy horses underwent histopathology and mineral microparticle analysis using electron microscopy and spectrometry (SEM/EDS). For each lung sample, mineral microparticles were counted and classified as endogenous or exogenous, the latter classified as geogenic or anthropogenic. Owners completed an environmental questionnaire. Mineral microparticle proportions (%), living conditions (indoors/outdoors), and exposures to environmental pollutants were compared between cases and controls. Correlations between mineral microparticle proportions and environmental variables were assessed. Mineral microparticles of both endogenous and exogenous origin were identified in all samples; geogenic particles were the most abundant. SiAlMgFe (iron-magnesium-aluminosilicate) proportion was higher in control (2.25%; Q1-Q3 1.85-9.27) compared to EqF-ILD (0%; Q1-Q3 0-0; p = 0.002) and idiopathic-EqF-ILD group (0%; Q1-Q3 0-0; p 0.05). FeCrNi and Feo (p = 0.004; R2 = 0.258; p < 0.001; R2 = 0.483) proportions were positively related to 'living indoors'. Retrospective collection of data, small number of cases. SEM/EDS successfully detected accumulation of inhaled mineral microparticles in the lung tissue of equids. A different distribution of geogenic and anthropogenic particles was identified between equids with EqF-ILD and controls.

title: Evolutionary Events Underlying Vector Competence and Epidemiological Variation in Hematophagous Diptera with Special Reference to Sand Flies and Mosquitoes.
abstract: Order Diptera includes house flies, blow flies, horse flies, midges, mosquitoes, sand flies, etc. Among these, mosquitoes and sand flies play a central role in the transmission of diseases affecting man and animals. They are typically characterised by a single pair of functional wings and a reduced, modified pair of halteres. Dipterans have evolved over 200 million years, undergoing extensive diversification shaped by adaptations in flight, sensory biology, feeding behaviour, and life history traits. Hematophagy is independently evolved in mosquitoes and sand flies, has been a key trait linked to reproductive success, while also facilitating pathogen transmission. The ability of this order of insects to transmit diseases/pathogens is referred as vector competence. It depends on complex interactions between vector genetics, microbiota, immune responses and environmental factors. It also involves multiple physiological barriers within the insect/vector. More than 150,000 species described are distributed across numerous genera and evolutionary lineages. Dipterans have well-defined synapomorphies, which include specialised mouthparts and complete metamorphosis, which have helped them to exploit diverse ecological niches. Understanding their evolutionary history and important biological traits underlying vector competence is crucial for explaining why only certain species efficiently transmit pathogens, parasites, bacteria and viruses. This kind of knowledge is crucial for improving vector surveillance, designing new control strategies, and targeted intervention for reducing the global burden of vector-borne diseases. Although many arthropods can carry pathogens incidentally, a limited number of these hematophagous insects act as consistent and efficient disease vectors. Hence, play a crucial role in the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases. Successful transmission of the pathogen depends predominantly on vector competence. This reflects the genetic compatibility between the pathogen and the arthropod vector, as most ingested pathogens are killed during blood meal digestion. The broader concept of vectorial capacity and vectorial competence is shaped largely by complex interactions with the vector, host, pathogen, environment, and the arthropod-associated microbiota. This significantly influences host morphology and transmission efficiency. Notably, vectorial capacity is not a static phenomenon; it varies across time and space, thereby altering host-pathogen transmission dynamics/cycles. Feeding behaviour is attributed to transmission dynamics, like anthropophilic mosquitoes, e.g. Aedes spp. exhibit more susceptibility to viral infections as they predominantly feed on humans. Hematophagy/blood feeding occurs at different life stages across insect/vector taxa, with only female mosquitoes now requiring blood meals. In addition to blood, mosquitoes also rely heavily on plant sap sugars for survival. Contemporary climate change and biological invasions are expanding vector distributions. Thus, increasing disease risk in previously unaffected areas/populations, underscoring the critical need for a deeper understanding of the triad of vector-pathogen-environment interactions. This review addresses this triad and the evolution of this character in dipterans.

title: An equine bone marrow aspirate concentrate protocol yields a predictable cellular and cytokine profile.
abstract: Bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) is a quick, minimally invasive, point-of-care therapy for equine orthopaedic injuries. Despite growing clinical use, standardised manufacturing methods are lacking, and the final product remains poorly characterised. To develop a reproducible protocol for equine BMAC production that yields predictable cellular and cytokine compositions. In vitro analytical study. Bone marrow aspirate (BMA) was harvested from the sternum of eight healthy adult horses and filtered to remove possible bony spicules. After centrifugation at 1000 × g for 10 min, the buffy coat was collected to generate BMAC. Cellular composition was assessed using standard haematology and cytology, and cytokine concentrations were measured using commercially available enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits. Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation. BMA filtration successfully removed potential bony material without significantly altering the cellular profile. Cells were predictably concentrated in BMAC: total nucleated cells increased from 77 ± 30 × 103/μL to 240 ± 57 × 103/μL; and platelets from 119 ± 34 × 103/μL to 269 ± 81 × 103/μL. Anti-inflammatory cytokines were increased in BMAC: IL-1ra increased from 18,611.3 ± 5509.1 to 36,598.8 ± 5971.8 pg/mL; IL-10 from 9.0 ± 7.5 to 19.1 ± 15.6 ng/mL; and TGF-β1 from 2535.0 ± 3018.7 to 5073.8 ± 2175.9 pg/mL. Of the pro-inflammatory cytokines measured, only IL-1β was increased (287.5 ± 22.5 to 475.1 ± 206.0 pg/mL), while TNF-α and IL-6 were unchanged. The small cohort size (n = 8) limited sensitivity for detecting minor effects. The cytokine panel, while representative, does not encompass all potential bioactive mediators, and single-time-point measurements do not necessarily reflect in vivo release kinetics. The clinical efficacy of BMAC was not evaluated, preventing direct correlation between compositional features and therapeutic outcomes. The BMAC protocol yielded consistently concentrated nucleated cells, preserved cellular morphology, and enhanced the anti-inflammatory cytokine profile relative to post-filtration BMA. These findings provide a biological rationale for intra-articular and intra-lesional use of BMAC in equine patients.

title: Perioperative complications in hospitalized horses: validation of a severity classification system in a cohort of 1207 surgical cases (2005-2025).
abstract: Perioperative complications (POC) are increasingly relevant in equine surgery as they affect hospitalization time, costs, morbidity and mortality rates. Identification and classification of POC is of paramount importance as they can be used as a surgical outcome measure. In equine practice, there are neither widely accepted definitions nor comprehensive severity classification systems for POC to allow comparison between studies and institutions. Moreover, transparent reporting of hospital POC trends is lacking. This study aims to: (i) describe the prevalence and distribution of POC occurring in a single equine hospital; (ii) propose and validate a scalable, 6-grade, severity-based, systematic, and objective POC classification system. A total of 1306 surgical procedures (both elective and non-elective) performed on 1207 independent surgical cases over 20 years (2005-2025) were retrospectively reviewed and included in the study. A total of 424 POC, defined as any deviation from the expected perioperative course, were recorded after 330 procedures. Overall, one or more POC occurred in 25.3% (IC 95%: 22.9%, 27.6%) procedures. The overall incidence rate of POC was 45.3 complications per 1000 horse-hospitalization days (95% CI: 41.01, 49.63).Considering the 6-grade severity-based system (grades I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IV, V), in which POC are classified based on the intervention required for treatment - from grade I requiring only minor interventions to grade V resulting in death or euthanasia - 32.3% POC were scored as grade I, 22.9% as grade II, 15.3% as grade IIIa, 8.5% as grade IIIb, 8.0% as grade IV, and 13.0% as grade V. Based on risk areas, 29.2% POC were considered surgery-related, 37.7% procedure-specific, 7.8% anaesthesia-related, 21.2% hospitalization-related and 4.0% drug-related. The most frequently reported POC were surgical site infection (3.6%), suture dehiscence (2.9%), diarrhoea (2.68%), and jugular thrombophlebitis (2.06%). The POC classification system proposed was validated by correlating POC severity scoring and hospitalization time in a cohort of studied cases (n=253, ρ = 0.42, p < 0.001), also after adjusting for surgical urgency (elective and non-elective cases) and anatomical system involved. This study characterises POC across all surgical procedures performed in a single equine hospital, proposing and validating a scalable classification system for POC severity. The implementation of these findings across different institutions may constitute a valuable step towards shared and repeatable clinical auditing in equine practice.

title: Wearable sensing technologies and machine learning for fatigue assessment in sport horses.
abstract: Fatigue in sport horses is a multifactorial phenomenon that critically affects performance, injury risk, and welfare, yet its real-time, field-based assessment remains an unmet challenge. To synthesise evidence on the use of wearable sensors and machine learning for fatigue-related monitoring in sport horses and to identify priorities for future fatigue assessment. Scoping review. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Publications from 2015 to 2026 were identified through Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect. Evidence from 102 publications was synthesised across five sensing modalities-heart rate (HR)/heart rate variability (HRV), thermometry, inertial measurement units (IMUs), surface electromyography (sEMG), and GPS-alongside machine learning applications for feature extraction, state classification, and risk modelling. Our synthesis reveals a fundamental disconnect: while each technology captures distinct physiological or biomechanical correlates of load, including autonomic response, thermoregulatory strain, gait stability, neuromuscular activation, and external workload, none provides a standalone signature of fatigue. Only a minority of studies used fatigue as a direct modelling label, with most relying on proxy outcomes such as asymmetry or performance decrement. The included literature was heterogeneous in sensor modalities, study designs, outcome measures, and application contexts. In addition, the limited use of directly defined fatigue outcomes restricted comparison across studies and constrained conclusions regarding fatigue-specific monitoring. The path forward lies not in developing yet another single-sensor solution, but in establishing a multidimensional, context-aware framework that integrates complementary data streams, individualised baselines, and interpretable models. Future research should prioritise: (1) operationalised fatigue definitions; (2) longitudinal, within-horse monitoring designs; (3) robust multimodal fusion architectures; (4) rigorous external validation across equestrian disciplines; and (5) explainable artificial intelligence to bridge the gap between algorithmic output and actionable training decisions.

title: Duodenal mucosal macrophages and their role in equine inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: Intestinal macrophages are key regulators of gastrointestinal immune homeostasis and inflammation, yet their distribution, polarisation, and role in equine inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remain poorly defined. (1) To assess agreement between duodenal endoscopic biopsies and paired full-thickness samples for macrophage quantification; (2) To compare duodenal macrophage polarisation between horses with and without IBD. Postmortem comparative study and case-control clinical study. Duodenal biopsies and paired full-thickness duodenal tissues were collected postmortem from 5 horses. Duodenal biopsies were performed by gastroscopy in 29 client-owned horses (IBD and control). Pan-macrophages (Iba-1) and M2 macrophages (CD204) were quantified by immunohistochemistry and histomorphometry within predefined mucosal regions. Agreement between biopsy and paired tissue was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Group comparisons were performed using linear mixed models or non-parametric tests. Duodenal biopsies underestimated macrophage counts. Agreement was moderate for CD204-positive macrophages across most mucosal regions (ICC 0.71-0.73; p = 0.001). Agreement for Iba-1-positive macrophages was poor, reaching significance only in the basal deep lamina propria (ICC = 0.50; p = 0.02). Horses with IBD had higher Iba-1-positive macrophage counts in the villous (70.4 ± 24.0 vs. 42.4 ± 18.1; p = 0.003) and total lamina propria (56.5 ± 23.3 vs. 38.8 ± 16.0; p = 0.03). M1 macrophage counts were greater in IBD horses in the villous (60.1 ± 5.1 vs. 20.9 ± 12.3; p = 0.002), total (48.0 ± 5.5 vs. 24.4 ± 8.5; p = 0.02), and sub-cryptal lamina propria (49.0 ± 9.4 vs. 18.6 ± 8.8; p = 0.03). Small sample size, no equine-specific M1 markers, and biopsy quality. Horses with IBD have significantly higher numbers of duodenal mucosal macrophages, highlighting their potential importance in the diagnostic interpretation and clinical management.

title: Comparative Plasma Proteomics of Arabian and Thoroughbred Racehorses at Rest and During Early Recovery from Training and Racing.
abstract: Breed-associated differences in the plasma proteome of Arabian and Thoroughbred racehorses at rest and during early recovery from training and racing remain incompletely characterised. Tandem mass tag (TMT)-based liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) plasma proteomics was performed on samples from 43 Thoroughbred and Arabian racehorses collected at rest and 30-40min post-exercise during early-season training, mid-season training, and racing. Breed and sex effects were tested with false discovery rate correction within each contrast and an effect-size threshold (absolute fold change >= 1.20); age and race placing were evaluated by breed- and time-specific Spearman correlations. More proteins met the reporting criteria for between-breed differences during initial training and racing than during mid-season training. Across the analysed contrasts, proteins with higher relative abundance in Arabians included FETUB, CNTN1, FGFR1, HGFAC and C4BPA, while proteins with lower abundance included ENPP5, SMPDL3B, KRT8 and KRT19. Age was associated with the plasma abundance of proteins annotated to coagulation, lipid transport, immune regulation and extracellular matrix-related functions. More proteins met the reporting criteria for sex-associated differences at rest than during early recovery. Exploratory associations with race placing were detected for two proteins in Thoroughbreds after exercise, with none meeting the reporting criteria in Arabians. These findings identify breed-associated plasma protein differences and candidates for independent validation.

title: Evaluation of Agreement Between Turnkey Markerless and Marker-Based Motion Capture Workflows During an Equine Odontoplasty.
journal: IISE transactions on occupational ergonomics and human factors
abstract: OCCUPATIONAL APPLICATIONSOpenCap and Vicon Nexus did not agree equally across body regions during a simulated equine odontoplasty. Lower extremity joint angles showed the best agreement, with hip flexion/adduction and knee movements generally within moderate-to-strong waveform agreement, while trunk and pelvis measures showed moderate agreement. In contrast, upper extremity joint angles showed negligible-to-weak agreement, including physically implausible values when the arms and hands were occluded for sustained periods. For ergonomics and human factors practice, these findings suggest that turnkey markerless motion capture may be useful for screening lower extremity and some whole-body posture patterns when camera visibility is good, but it should not be relied on for detailed upper extremity assessment in tasks with frequent occlusion, tool use, or constrained working spaces. Practitioners considering markerless systems for field use should evaluate camera placement, expected occlusions, and whether the task requires coarse posture screening or precise joint angle measurement before using the data to support ergonomic decisions.

title: Factors associated with Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses in Europe (2022-2025).
abstract: Equine granulocytic anaplasmosis (EGA) is caused by Anaplasma phagocytophilum and mainly transmitted by Ixodes persulcatus complex ticks, particularly I. ricinus in Europe. The study aimed to investigate factors associated with PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses. Equine samples from across Europe submitted to a laboratory between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results on EDTA blood and serology using immunofluorescence antibody test (IFAT) on serum or plasma were included. Multiple logistic regression analysis was performed, in which horses were grouped in different age categories. Of 2,753 horses tested by PCR, 358 (13.0%) were positive. In the multivariable model, PCR positivity was associated with season, sampling year, European region, age category, sex, and horse type classification. The strongest seasonal effect was observed in winter, with lower odds compared to spring (OR=0.033, P18 years (OR=1.640, P<0.001), and in heavy horses compared with warmbloods (OR=2.740, P<0.001). Descriptively, PCR-positivity was highest in summer and lowest in winter; adjusted pairwise comparisons confirmed significantly lower odds in winter compared with the other three seasons, in accordance with tick activity patterns. Further significant differences between different seasons were not noted. The increasing seropositivity with increasing age can be interpreted as higher risk for pathogen contact during life. Horse type-associated differences may reflect unmeasured differences in management, housing conditions, and vector exposure rather than intrinsic biological susceptibility. Given the multi-host ecology of A. phagocytophilum and the zoonotic potential of some genetic variants, equine infections are relevant from a One Health and All-species perspective.

title: Evaluation of the Parasympathetic Tone Activity monitor in horses anesthetized with different isoflurane concentrations.
abstract: Parasympathetic Tone Activity (PTA) monitoring has been proposed as an indicator of nociception during general anesthesia in veterinary medicine. However, the influence of anesthetic depth on PTA responses remains poorly characterized in horses. Ten healthy horses were anesthetized at three end-tidal isoflurane concentrations (FE'ISO; 0.9%, 1.2%, and 1.5%). After stabilization, standardized electrical nociceptive stimulation (SENS) was applied. Immediate (PTAi) and mean (PTAm) PTA indices, heart rate, and arterial blood pressures were recorded before, during, and after stimulation. Data were analyzed using generalized linear mixed models, cross-correlation, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. SENS significantly decreased PTAi and PTAm (p = 0.001), whereas FE'ISO had no significant effect (p = 0.818 and p = 0.915, respectively). PTAi decreased from 75 (95% CI: 73-77) to 48 (95% CI: 43-52), representing a 36% reduction. PTAi and PTAm reached their nadirs 1.2 and 2.2-2.7 min after stimulation, respectively. A significant FE'ISO × timepoint interaction was identified for PTAi (p = 0.001). MAP increased immediately after SENS and preceded PTAi decreases by 1.1 min. PTAi moderately identified cardiovascular responses to SENS (ROC AUC 0.707; 95% CI: 0.650-0.765). Overall, PTAi and PTAm responded to SENS across the FE'ISO concentrations evaluated; however, the moderate discriminative ability of PTAi indicated a limited relationship between PTA and mean arterial pressure.

title: Prevalence and genetic characterization of Cryptosporidium spp. and Enterocytozoon bieneusi in horses in central and western Inner Mongolia, China.
abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. and Enterocytozoon bieneusi are important enteric pathogens infecting humans and a wide range of animal hosts, including horses, and some species and genotypes have zoonotic significance. However, information on their prevalence and genetic characteristics in horses in Inner Mongolia remains limited. This study investigated the prevalence, species/genotype composition, and genetic diversity of Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi in horses from central and western Inner Mongolia. From May to September 2025, 325 horse fecal samples were collected from Otog Banner, Zhenglan Banner, and Abaga Banner, Inner Mongolia, China. Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi were detected by nested PCR targeting the SSU rRNA gene and ITS region, respectively. C. hominis-positive samples were further subtyped by gp60 amplification. Phylogenetic and haplotype analyses were performed to assess genetic relationships and diversity, and prevalence was compared among geographic, age, and health-status groups. The overall prevalence of Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi was 2.8% (9/325) and 1.5% (5/325), respectively. Two Cryptosporidium species were identified: C. hominis (55.6%, 5/9) and C. parvum (44.4%, 4/9). All C. hominis isolates belonged to the Ik subtype family, including IkA18G1 and IkA19G1. Cryptosporidium prevalence was significantly higher in foals than in adult horses (11.5% vs. 1.1%, p < 0.05) and in diarrheic than non-diarrheic horses (16.1% vs. 1.4%, p < 0.05). All E. bieneusi-sequences were identified as genotype horse1 and clustered within Group 1. Phylogenetic and haplotype analyses showed that the Cryptosporidium sequences were closely related to previously reported equid-derived sequences from China. C. hominis exhibited genetic diversity, whereas the E. bieneusi horse1 genotype showed a relatively conserved genetic structure. This study provides new molecular epidemiological and genetic insights into Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi in horses in central and western Inner Mongolia, including, the first regional report of the C. hominis gp60 subtype IkA19G1. The higher Cryptosporidium prevalence in foals and diarrheic horses highlights these groups as priorities for surveillance. These findings provide baseline information for future molecular surveillance and assessment of potential public health risks associated with these enteric pathogens in horses in this important horse-breeding region of China.

title: Pre-ride transport as a key modulating factor of plasma metabolites and performance-related physiological abilities in Arabian endurance horses.
abstract: Endurance competitions impose high metabolic and physiological demands on horses, requiring precise regulation of energy metabolism, hydration, and stress responses. Transport before competition is a recognised stressor capable of altering biochemical and hormonal balance, potentially influencing readiness for prolonged exercise. Understanding how arrival timing affects metabolic status may improve both performance and welfare in endurance horses. To determine whether the timing of pre-ride transport modulates baseline plasma metabolite profiles and post-exercise metabolic responses in Arabian endurance horses competing over 80 km. Observational field study. Ten Arabian horses were divided into two groups to compare horses arriving 1 day before competition (Tr1; n = 5) with those transported on the day of the ride (Tr2; n = 5). Blood samples collected before and after the ride were used for untargeted liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry metabolomic analyses. Baseline metabolomics revealed increased oxidative-stress-related metabolites in Tr2 and higher carnitine-associated metabolites in Tr1. Following the ride, Tr1 exhibited stronger increases in lipid-oxidation and amino-acid-catabolism metabolites, whereas Tr2 showed attenuated fold changes, consistent with reduced metabolic flexibility and incomplete recovery from transport stress. Limited sample size. Arrival timing significantly modulates metabolic baseline and substrate-utilisation responses in endurance Arabian horses. Allowing at least 1 day of recovery after transport may enhance physiological stability, metabolic adaptability, and overall performance readiness.

title: Bacterial Isolates and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Profiles in Mares with Endometritis in Zhangye, China.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Equine endometritis impairs fertility, but regional data remain scarce in Zhangye, Gansu Province, China, a major production base for equine serum-derived biological products. This cross-sectional study investigated endometritis and associated bacterial isolates in 985 mares from five intensive horse farms. Mares with reproductive abnormalities underwent clinical, ultrasonographic, and cytological evaluation. Laboratory investigations included culture of low-volume uterine flush samples, biochemical testing, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Among the 156 mares selected for further evaluation, 35 were diagnosed with endometritis. This corresponded to an apparent prevalence of 3.6% in the full surveyed population (35/985; 95% confidence interval, 2.5-4.9%) and a detection rate of 22.4% in the selected subgroup (35/156; 95% confidence interval, 16.2-29.8%). Clinical manifestations were generally subtle. Thirty culture-positive samples yielded 38 isolates across six genera. Escherichia coli, Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus, and Staphylococcus aureus predominated. A single bacterial taxon was recovered from 22 (73.3%) culture-positive mares, whereas multiple bacterial taxa were recovered from eight (26.7%). Escherichia and Streptococcus isolates showed relatively high resistance, whereas Staphylococcus and Bacillus isolates exhibited lower overall resistance. Limited geographical coverage, small isolate numbers, incomplete antimicrobial-use records, and unexamined resistance genes constrained interpretation. These findings support early screening of mares with reproductive disorders and antimicrobial selection guided by culture and susceptibility testing.

title: Pharmacokinetics of Sulfasalazine and the Temporal Profiles of Sulfapyridine and Its Metabolites Following Nasogastric Administration in Six Healthy Adult Horses.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Sulfasalazine is an azo-linked prodrug of sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid that is activated by bacterial azoreductases in the distal gut. Its disposition has not been described in horses, in which extensive hindgut fermentation may influence prodrug activation. This study characterised the concentration-time profile of sulfasalazine and the appearance of sulfapyridine, 5-hydroxy-sulfapyridine and N4-acetyl-sulfapyridine after a single oral dose. Six healthy adult Warmblood horses received sulfasalazine (16 mg/kg) by nasogastric tube, and blood was sampled hourly for 14 h. Sulfasalazine and sulfapyridine were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry; both metabolites were assessed semi-quantitatively as peak-area ratios. Sulfasalazine was measurable from 1 h and reached a median maximum concentration of 386.61 ng/mL (Q1-Q3 330.44-504.35) at a median of 5.5 h, then declined steeply. Sulfapyridine remained near the limit of detection for six hours, rose abruptly between 7 and 8 h and peaked at a median of 2794.00 ng/mL (2381.87-3146.14) at 9.0 h, approximately seven-fold above the parent-drug maximum. Both metabolites rose in parallel with sulfapyridine. This timing matches published equine orocaecal transit times, indicating that sulfasalazine reaches the hindgut largely intact and is activated there by microbial azoreduction. Systemic sulfapyridine exposure was substantial and should be considered in any therapeutic use.

title: Analysis of Factors Affecting Pregnancy Rate After Artificial Insemination in Lusitano Broodmares.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Artificial insemination (AI) is widely used in the horse breeding industry, but its success is often limited by different factors. Our objective was to assess the importance of various factors affecting fertility after AI, using field data collected in 125 mares over a period of 20 years, corresponding to a total of 860 mare-year combinations. The criteria defined for measuring fertility were: (1) pregnancy rate per breeding season; (2) pregnancy diagnosed at the 14th day on the first cycle and (3) number of cycles needed for a mare to become pregnant. Statistical analyses were performed using the GLIMMIX procedure of SAS, with a binary logit model with repeated records. The overall pregnancy rate per breeding season (PRBS) was 0.813 and at 14 days on the first cycle (PR1C) it was 0.546. The PRBS was higher when insemination was practiced early in the breeding season (p < 0.001) and declined with increasing mare age (p < 0.001) as well as with stallion age (p = 0.013). Mares presenting uterine pre-AI oedema had higher fertility at PR1C (p = 0.037). The mean number of oestrous cycles for a confirmed pregnancy was 1.82 ± 1.01 and, among others, age impacted this result adversely. In conclusion, our results suggest that some identified key factors can be used by owners, farm managers and veterinarians to improve mare reproductive performance.

title: Whole-Genome Characterization of a G3P[59] Rotavirus A Strain from a Diarrheic Donkey Foal Reveals an Unusual Genomic Background.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Rotavirus A (RVA) is an important enteric pathogen of neonatal animals, whereas the genomic diversity of donkey-origin RVA remains incompletely defined. In 2025, an RVA strain was recovered from a diarrheic donkey foal in Shandong Province, China, and designated RVA/Donkey-wt/CHN/SD2503/2025/G3P[59] (SD2503). Viral RNA was subjected to Illumina NovaSeq paired-end sequencing, de novo assembly, genotype assignment, sequence comparison, and segment-specific maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis. Sequences corresponding to all 11 genome segments were recovered, yielding the constellation G3-P[59]-I3-R3-C3-M3-A9-N3-T3-E3-H6. The VP4 gene was highly divergent: the closest BLASTn match was the P[24] rhesus strain TUCH, with 79.58% nucleotide identity, below the 80% threshold used to assign VP4 sequences to the same P genotype. The VP4 sequence was subsequently confirmed by the Rotavirus Classification Working Group as P[59]. Other segments showed discordant relationships. VP7 clustered with rabbit strain rab1404 with strong bootstrap support, whereas several internal genes grouped within genotype backgrounds represented by simian, rabbit, pangolin, equine, and other mammalian RVAs. The topological incongruence across segments, together with the unusual genotype constellation, suggests possible historical reassortment involving cross-species-associated RVA lineages, although the specific reassortment events remain unresolved. SD2503 provides an 11-segment genomic framework for an independently identified donkey G3P[59] RVA and supports broader genomic surveillance of RVA in equids.

title: Polypropylene Mesh-Augmented Soft-Tissue Reconstruction for Presumed Traumatic Lateral Patellar Luxation in an Adult Pony: A Case Report.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Patellar luxation is uncommon in horses, and traumatic lateral luxation in adult equids has rarely been reported. A 3-year-old, 75 kg female Shetland pony presented with severe right hindlimb lameness and minimal weight bearing approximately 2 weeks after a suspected traumatic event. The right patella was fixed lateral to the femoral trochlea and could not be manually reduced during conscious examination.
